authoringNote: The SOURCE and the rule were authored first (a type name is a single-line dotted name; grammar recovery must never turn a text slice into a type), but the expectation JSON was written after measuring, so the flag says so rather than claiming otherwise. The measured value it pins is the one the rule predicts (Integer on line 8), and the welded text below is a regression I introduced and then measured — see the source comment.
rationale: M60 R10 follow-up, the recovery half of the scoped-type fix. Admitting `scoped_type_identifier` into the declared-reference collectors introduced a REGRESSION, caught by the census on a real corpus file rather than by any fixture: grails-scaffolding's templates/scaffolding/AsyncController.groovy opens with an ERB-style `<%= ... %>` placeholder and then `import static org.springframework.http.HttpStatus.*` followed by another import. Under recovery the pinned grammar welds those two statements into ONE nested scoped_type_identifier chain whose outermost node spans both lines and contains an ERROR node (`ERROR="*\nimport"`), so the outermost node's TEXT is `org.springframework.http.HttpStatus.*` + newline + `import org.springframework.transaction.TransactionStatus`. The new branch published `n.text`, so this file emitted a declared_type reference whose target was that whole slice — a string that appears nowhere in the source as a name, spanning two statements, carrying `*` and the keyword `import`. That is a fabrication of exactly the kind this project refuses, and it is why the rule now lives where text becomes a name: a type name is dots and identifier characters ON ONE LINE (`isPlainTypeName`), and the branch STOPS when the text fails that test instead of falling back to descending — its segments are the very fabrication the scoped-type-references fixture forbids. Measured on the census sample (800 groovy files from grails-core + geb): that weld was the only non-name target in the whole declared-position edge set, 1 of 87 written qualified types, and the predicate is provably INERT on every well-formed name (the census dump after the guard differs from the dump before it by exactly that one row). What this fixture must therefore show: the malformed pair of imports contributes NO declared-type edge in any spelling (not the welded slice, not its qualifier segments, not the leaf), and the one declared type genuinely written in the file — the `Integer` parameter on line 8 — is still published. Disclosure: this file also shows the lane's KNOWN owed `calls` class (an interpolated string and the template placeholder `Controller` published as juxt call targets, groovy's conviction in validation/m60/target-spelling-register.json). That class is owned and tracked by the register, not by this fixture, so it is neither pinned nor forbidden here.

expectRelationships.note: the ONE type actually written in the file, still published — the refusal must not take a well-formed name with it
